scope_note: Conservative evidence-bounded inventory. This revision narrows completed conclusions to named studies, separates Meta-Surgeon ranking, transfer, calibration, active learning, OOD, continual learning, and constrained autonomy, pins newly inspected source implementations, and tracks independent compatibility axes. New scope may lower scores; source discovery does not imply support.

scope_history.change: Initial grouped evidence-based inventory; preserve identifiers and append discoveries.
Narrowed six conclusions to exact report scopes; split Meta-Surgeon decision/transfer/calibration/active-learning/OOD/continual/autonomy objectives and added explicit milestone research questions.

milestones.title: Leakage and provenance audit for v0.8 evidence
milestones.description: Audit the recorded v0.8 Meta-Surgeon splits, model grouping, provenance, and retention of negative outcomes.
milestones.scope: The documented v0.8 dataset/split audit in the named v0.5/v1.0 records only; this does not conclude data quality or representativeness across all models, tasks, or future corpora.
acceptance_criteria: The named reports record model-grouped train/validation/test boundaries and retain negative/rejected outcomes with provenance.
milestones.remaining_work: Expand audits to independently collected physical outcomes across model families, task domains, hardware, distributions, and future training data.
limitations: Closes only the audited v0.8 evidence records; it does not validate future corpora, broad distributions, or every contamination pathway.

history.reason: Initial conservative assessment against the pinned main commit.
Narrowed conclusion to the exact named evidence scope; broader questions remain open separately.

research_questions: Do the audited v0.8 records separate model/component train, validation, and held-out test examples and retain source identity, negative outcomes, and reproduction metadata?

milestones.title: Q1–Q3 static, activation, and gradient feature ablations
milestones.description: Evaluate the static, activation, and gradient feature profiles used by the v0.8 candidate predictor on named small checkpoint cells.
milestones.scope: Q1–Q3 ablations on three named sub-billion checkpoints and their persisted component split protocol. Hessian, hardware-conditioned, cross-family, quantized, and future representations remain outside this closed study.
acceptance_criteria: Q1–Q3 reports preserve paired feature ablations, model/split identities, uncertainty, and per-profile negative, inconclusive, and positive findings.
milestones.remaining_work: Study architecture-aware, hardware-conditioned, quantized, curvature, and interaction features on independent data; do not infer those results from Q1–Q3.
limitations: Q1–Q3 cover three named small models and one short calibration corpus; they do not establish cross-domain or physical optimizer advantage.

history.reason: Initial conservative assessment against the pinned main commit.
Narrowed conclusion to the exact named evidence scope; broader questions remain open separately.
Reassessed the bounded Q1-Q3 aggregate: Q1 was negative, Q2 inconclusive, and Q3 predictive metrics improved; the combined result is mixed, not wholly negative.

research_questions: On the three Q1–Q3 checkpoint cells, do static, activation, and gradient profiles improve held-out candidate safety/quality prediction over their declared controls?

milestones.title: Q4 held-out single-channel learned ranking versus controls
milestones.description: Test whether the v0.8 learned candidate ranker selects safer single-channel masks than random and magnitude at matched budget.
milestones.scope: Exact Q4 evaluation over 51 component-held-out candidates per model, 20 paired seeds, three named checkpoints, and ΔPPL ≤ 0.01. Not cumulative surgery, end-to-end optimization, or broad transfer.
acceptance_criteria: Q4 reproduces paired equal-budget selections, threshold violations, ΔPPL uncertainty, exact IDs, and its single-mask boundary.
milestones.remaining_work: Test cumulative physical surgery, reloadable artifact quality, size, inference, memory, and optimization cost at equal budget.
limitations: Positive candidate-ranking evidence covers single-channel masks on three checkpoints; deployed artifact gains are unmeasured.

history.reason: Initial conservative assessment against the pinned main commit.
Narrowed conclusion to the exact named evidence scope; broader questions remain open separately.

research_questions: At Q4's equal budget and split, does the learned ranker select a set with lower measured single-mask ΔPPL and fewer quality violations than random and magnitude?

milestones.title: Kronecker-factored structured sensitivity
milestones.description: Bounded KFAC second-moment collection and local structured-removal cost estimation, followed by coupled MLP candidate evaluation and optional compensation.
milestones.scope: Trace LLM-Surgeon KFAC; independently score row and column removals from raw activation and output-gradient second moments; collect factors within memory budgets; aggregate coupled gate/up/down MLP channel costs; optionally compensate surviving weights; evaluate physical held-out outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: The KFAC row and column quadratic score agrees with dense Kronecker Hessian calculations on deterministic small cases, including grouped removals and invalid numerical inputs.

A bounded collector records raw second moments from independent calibration observations, reports its planned workspace bound, observation counts, numerical checks, and provenance, and is later measured for peak process memory during a physical run.
An architecture adapter scores all coupled projections for one explicitly named Hugging Face MLP architecture without mutating weights or bypassing the optimization orchestrator.
At equal physical parameter removal, repeated held-out comparisons include no-repair KFAC, random seeds, magnitude, activation, and first-order gradient baselines under the existing quality gate.

Every passing artifact reloads successfully; quality uncertainty, optimization time, peak RAM/VRAM, artifact bytes, and inference outcomes are recorded. Compensation is assessed as a separate arm and never inferred from uncorrected scores.

evidence_refs.label: Uncompensated CPU KFAC row/column cost prototype
Dense Kronecker parity and input/budget tests
Collector masking, bounds, transactional update, and scorer integration tests

milestones.remaining_work: Wire the bounded collector to model forward/backward hooks for one named architecture; collect independent calibration observations; add coupled MLP channel aggregation and optimizer integration behind an architecture adapter; run a small pinned pretrained CPU evaluation before any hardware-scale study.
limitations: The collector accepts caller-fed activations and output gradients; it is not wired to model hooks, a named architecture adapter, or calibration-split provenance.
The scorer computes only uncompensated linear row/column group costs; it does not represent coupled gate/up/down channel removal.
Workspace is conservatively preflighted, not measured peak process or system memory.
No pretrained model result, physical artifact result, quality gain, runtime gain, or memory gain exists.
The upstream implementation supports only its traced OPT/LLaMA paths and uses an older framework stack; no universal architecture support is implied.

research_sources.licence_note: Pinned root LICENSE is MIT; no source copied. Preserve notice on future reuse. Model artifacts have separate upstream licenses.
research_sources.method: Compares routing frequency/mass, output norm, REAP, random and contrastive expert scores; adds paired masked ablation, byte-preserving GGUF expert surgery, and optional distillation repair.
research_sources.relevance: Directly relevant to PRs #736/#738 and quantized MoE optimization; retains random controls and explicit negative expert-selection findings.
research_sources.integration_approach: ADAPT score baselines and artifact invariants behind existing GGUF/architecture boundaries after independent reproduction; preserve attribution if code is reused.
research_sources.hypothesis: Router-only scores can suppress general-coverage experts; interaction or causal diagnostics may identify safer sets, while deep pruning may lose to equal-memory low-bit quantization.
research_sources.requirements: Pinned README reports runs on DGX Spark with 119GB unified memory. Tiny synthetic MoE tests and CPU fixture validation may be feasible; model-scale results are not GPU-feasible on the current 12GB card.
research_sources.findings: Inspected scoring.py, ablation.py, gguf_prune.py, surgery.py, tests and MIT LICENSE. Upstream reports a contrastive collapse, byte-preserving GGUF edits, and pruning-vs-quantization results; these are not independently reproduced here.
